title: Whip Pan
description: A whip pan pans so quickly that the image blurs into horizontal streaks, then snaps to a new composition. Two shots can be joined inside compatible directional motion blur, creating the impression of one fast reorientation.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The move is a transition, a punchline, or a sudden shift of attention. Energy transfers between spaces that may not even be adjacent.
An ordinary change of location can feel like a comic snap if the blur matches. It is the wrong tool for a readable pan across a mural, and the wrong tool if you need to see the travel.
If the landing is not sharp, the whip is only a smear.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Match blur direction, luminance, duration, and acceleration if you cut inside the blur. Design the sharp landing before generating the two sides.
Opposite pan directions or mismatched brightness expose the seam. Prompt a violent whip pan off the subject, horizontal motion blur streaking the world, then a snap resolve on the next beat.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it as a transition, punchline, or sudden attention shift. Concrete beat: a look off, a blur, a new room already in progress.
Do not whip across information the audience must read.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Pan Left or Pan Right stays readable. A Whip Tilt is the same idea on the pitch axis.
A Crash Zoom In blurs radially by changing focal length, not by yaw. Whip pan is horizontal speed past recognition, then a hard stop.
Whip TiltVertical shock instead of a horizontal whip.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Shaun of the Dead compresses routine and travel with fast visual joins. Hot Fuzz accelerates exposition with whip-like moves.
Baby Driver and Whiplash time the blur to music and hits. Use the matched smear and the landing, not the playlist.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Violent whip pan off [Subject], horizontal motion blur streaking the world into ribbons, then a snap resolve on the next beat. For motion: extremely fast whip pan away from [Subject], heavy horizontal motion blur, then a sharp stop.

Generate A: a baker turns toward a ringing telephone and the camera whip-pans right into horizontal blur. Generate B: begin with the same rightward blur and land on a flour-covered delivery driver outside. Join at maximum blur. Keep motion direction and brightness compatible; no dissolve.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a fast Pan Right that never blurs, or a Crash Zoom In. The tell is readable detail in the middle, radial zoom blur, or a seam where blur directions disagree.
The fix: commit to unreadability in the middle, match the join, stop sharp.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Whip Pan in film?
It is a pan so fast that the frame becomes horizontal motion blur, often used to hide a cut or to sting a new composition.
Whip Pan vs Crash Zoom In
Crash zoom in changes focal length and blurs radially. Whip pan rotates the camera on yaw and blurs sideways, then resolves on a new aim.
When should I use Whip Pan?
When you need a snap of attention or an invisible join between two setups. Do not use it to show a landscape.
How do I prompt Whip Pan for AI image or video?
Demand extremely fast horizontal pan, heavy motion blur, then a sharp stop on a named landing. If used as a cut, match blur direction on both sides.
